items.story: The loop is the round apple, the long stroke is its stick, and the short bar on top is the paper twist.
items.pic: A red toffee apple behind the bottom loop; the long vertical stroke is its wooden stick; a small paper twist on the top bar.
items.pt: In Portugal it is a maçã do amor.
items.sound: Like the Portuguese stressed **a** in *casa*: open and short.
items.tip: あ has no dot. お has a dot and its loop opens to the right.

items.story: Two eels rise side by side out of the water. The left one is a little taller and curls at the bottom.
items.pic: Two eels: give each stroke a tiny eye at the top end and small fins; a gentle water line near the bottom.
items.sound: Like Portuguese **i** in *ilha*.
items.tip: い has two similar strokes. In り the right stroke is much longer.

items.story: Someone bows so deeply it hurts. The dash is their head, and the curve is their bent back and legs.
items.pic: A bowing person in profile: a round head at the top dash; the curved stroke is the body bent forward; small motion lines of pain.
items.sound: Lips relaxed and not rounded, softer than the Portuguese **u** in *uva*.
items.tip: う has a flat dash on top. ら has a tick, and its stroke drops straight down before curving.

items.story: The dash is the dancer's head. The zigzag is the body and arm, and the sweep at the bottom is a kicking foot.
items.pic: A dancer: small head circle on the dash, the zigzag as body, ribbon trailing from the final sweep.
items.sound: Between the Portuguese **ê** and **é**.
items.tip: え has a separate dash on top. そ is one zigzag stroke.

items.story: It is the toffee apple from あ, but a worm (the dot) has popped out of the side. **Oh!**
items.pic: Same toffee apple idea as あ; the dot top-right is a little green worm peeking out.
items.sound: Between the Portuguese **ô** and **ó**.
items.tip: お has the dot (the worm). あ has none.

items.hook: A mosquito, which in Japanese is called **ka** (蚊).
items.story: The big hook is the mosquito's wing and body. The little dash is the whine of its buzz.
items.pic: A mosquito: body along the hooked stroke, translucent wing, long thin legs; the dash shown as a buzz line.
items.tip: か has a little extra dash. Katakana カ does not.

items.story: The two crossbars are the key's teeth, the long stroke is its shaft, and the curve at the bottom is the ring.
items.pic: An antique brass key: a ring around the bottom curve, teeth at the crossbars.
items.sound: In handwriting the bottom curve is often separate, as in the font shown here.
items.tip: き has two bars. さ has one.

items.story: A single bent stroke: the open beak of a cuckoo calling **ku-ku**.
items.pic: A cuckoo bird's head where the stroke is its open beak; eye and a few feathers.
items.pt: The cuckoo is *cuco* in Portuguese. It even sounds like **ku**-ko.
items.tip: く points left. へ is a hill, and points up.

items.story: Two strands of kelp. The short one on the left and the tall one on the right sway, and a fish (the bar) swims across.
items.pic: Green kelp along both vertical strokes, the horizontal bar as a small fish, bubbles.
items.tip: け has a tall right stroke. は has a loop at the bottom.

items.story: The two strokes are the upper and lower wings of a little biplane, flown by two **co**-pilots.
items.pic: Biplane seen from the front-side: the two strokes are the wings, add a small fuselage between them and a propeller.
items.tip: こ is two strokes. に has an extra stroke on the left.

items.story: The curve at the bottom is a wide-open mouth, and the cross is the dentist's mirror going in.
items.pic: A face in profile with the bottom curve as the open jaw; the crossing strokes as a dental mirror.
items.tip: さ has a curve that opens to the right. ち curves the other way, like a chin.

items.hook: **She** caught a fish on her hook.
items.story: A single fishing hook. **She** has just caught a fish on it.
items.pic: A fishing line coming down to the hook; a small fish dangling from the curl.
items.sound: Close to Portuguese **x** in *xícara*, but softer.
items.tip: し curls right. つ is a wave lying on its side.

items.story: The bar is a tree branch. The rope comes down and loops into a seat, then swings off to the side.
items.pic: A tree branch on the horizontal stroke, the loop as a swing seat, motion lines.
items.tip: す has a loop in the middle. む has its loop at the bottom left.

items.story: The long bar is the cathedral's roofline, and the two upright strokes are its twin towers rising above it.
items.pic: Facade of Lisbon Cathedral: the two vertical strokes are the twin towers with crenellations; small rose window and arched door under the bar.
items.pt: Lisbon's cathedral, the Sé, has two towers, and *sé* sounds just like **se**.
items.tip: Katakana セ is almost the same shape.

items.story: A long noodle zigzags off the chopsticks at the top and curls down into the bowl.
items.pic: Chopsticks at the top lifting the zigzag noodle; a bowl at the bottom where the curve lands, steam.
items.tip: そ zigzags. ろ is a smooth road.

items.story: The left part is a cross, like a **t**. The right part is a little **a**-shape. Together they spell **ta**.
items.pic: Subtle letter hints: a lowercase 't' ghosted over the left cross, an 'a' ghosted beside the right strokes.
items.tip: た has two parts. な has a loop.

items.story: A face in profile with a big **chi**n sticking out to the right, smiling for the camera.
items.pic: Profile of a smiling face: the bottom curve is the cheek and chin; small eye; a camera flash spark.
items.sound: Like the Portuguese **tch** in *tchau*.
items.tip: ち's chin sticks out to the right. さ opens its mouth to the right.

items.story: One big wave curls over and crashes.
items.pic: A curling ocean wave along the stroke with foam spray; a tiny boat underneath.
items.sound: Like the **ts** in *tsé-tsé*, then a soft u.
items.tip: つ is one curved wave. し is a hook.

items.story: The bar is an arm reaching out, and the curve is the hand cupping down.
items.pic: An arm along the top stroke ending in an open hand at the curve.
items.tip: て is one stroke. と has a little thorn on top.

items.hook: A **toe** with a thorn in it.
items.story: The curve is a big **toe**, and the short dash is the thorn stuck in it. Ouch!
items.pic: A foot/toe outline along the curve; the dash is a thorn; small 'ouch' lines.
items.tip: と has a thorn. て does not.

items.story: The loop at the bottom right is the tart seen from above. The cross is a cinnamon stick, and the dash is a sprinkle of sugar.
items.pic: A golden custard tart with caramelised spots inside the bottom loop; the cross as a cinnamon stick.
items.tip: な has a loop. た does not.

items.hook: The right side is 二, 'two', read **ni**.
items.story: The two short strokes are literally 二 (**ni**, 'two'). The tall stroke on the left is a finger pointing at them.
items.pic: Highlight the two right strokes with a soft '2' badge; a pointing hand on the left stroke.
items.sound: Your tongue touches the palate a little, like the Portuguese **nh** in *vinho*.
items.tip: に has an extra left stroke. こ is just the two lines.

items.story: Noodles tangled up, with a little knot (the loop) at the end of the tail.
items.pic: A tangle of noodles along the strokes, the end loop tied like a knot, chopsticks.
items.tip: ぬ has the knot at the end. め has none.

items.story: The upright stroke is the cat's back. The rest curls round into a loop: its tail.
items.pic: A sitting cat: ears and face near the top of the vertical stroke, the loop is its tail.
items.tip: ね ends in a loop (tail). れ ends with a kick, and わ ends with a smooth curve.

items.story: One sweeping stroke makes a circle with a slash through it: **no** entry!
items.pic: A red prohibition sign echo: soft circle behind the stroke, slash emphasised.
items.tip: の is one stroke. め and ぬ have two.

items.story: The left stroke and the bar form a capital **H**, and the right side curls like a little **a**.
items.pic: Ghosted letter 'H' over the left part and 'a' over the right part.
items.sound: When it is the topic particle, は is read **wa**. That is why こんにちは is 'konnichi**wa**'.
items.tip: は has one bar on the right. ほ has two.

items.story: The whole stroke is a wide smile with a dimple on the left: **hee hee**!
items.pic: A face with the stroke as a broad grin; two eyes above, rosy cheeks.
items.sound: A breathy h, almost like the German *ich*.
items.tip: ひ is one stroke. Katakana ヒ is angular.

items.story: The middle stroke is the peak, and the dots on each side are clouds drifting past.
items.pic: Mount Fuji silhouette with snowcap behind the centre strokes; the side strokes as little clouds.
items.sound: Somewhere between f and h. Blow gently, as if cooling soup. Portuguese has no exact match.

items.story: A single slope up and down: a small hill you have to **he**ave yourself over.
items.pic: A grassy hill under the stroke with a little hiker at the peak.
items.sound: As a particle meaning 'towards', へ is read **e**.
items.tip: Hiragana へ and katakana ヘ are almost identical.

items.hook: **Ho ho ho!** は wearing Santa's hat.
items.story: It is は with an extra bar on top, closing it like Santa's hat. Santa says **ho**!
items.pic: A Santa hat sitting on the top bar of the right part; snow dots.
items.tip: ほ has two bars, like a hat. は has one.

items.story: The two bars are sails crossing the **ma**st, and the loop at the bottom is a coil of rope on deck.
items.pic: A small boat: the vertical stroke as the mast, bars as sails, the loop as coiled rope, waves.
items.tip: ま has two bars and a loop. よ has one bar.

items.story: The curl is the lobe of an ear, and the last stroke is an earring.
items.pic: An ear outline around the curl; small earring on the crossing stroke.
items.tip: み curls left and has a crossing stroke.

items.story: The loop is the cow's snout, the dot is an ear twitching, and the cross is its horns. **Moo!**
items.pic: A friendly cow: horns at the cross, snout at the loop, spots.
items.tip: む has a dot on the right. す does not.

items.story: The loop is an eye, and the crossing stroke is a long eyelash.
items.pic: An eye inside the loop with an iris and pupil; lashes along the crossing stroke.
items.tip: め has no knot at the end. ぬ does.

items.hook: A hook with two worms: **mo**re fish!
items.story: A fishing hook with two worms (the bars) on it. **Mo**re bait means **mo**re fish.
items.pic: A fishing hook along the main stroke with two wriggly worms at the bars.
items.tip: も has two bars on a hook. し is just the hook.

items.story: The big curved stroke is a sail full of wind, the long stroke is the mast, and the dash is a flag.
items.pic: A sailboat: the curved stroke as a billowing sail, the long stroke as the mast, a tiny flag on the dash, waves.
items.tip: Katakana ヤ is almost the same shape.

items.story: Japanese bathhouses hang a curtain with this very character on it. The shape is the steam rising from the bath.
items.pic: A noren curtain shape behind the character, steam swirls, maybe the hot spring symbol.
items.tip: ゆ has a loop crossed by a line. よ has a loop at the bottom.

items.story: The bar is a finger, the vertical stroke is the string, and the loop at the bottom is the **yo**-yo.
items.pic: A yo-yo disc at the loop, the string up the vertical, motion lines.
items.tip: よ has one bar. ま has two.

items.story: The frog sits up tall. The tick on top is its eye, and the curve is its round body.
items.pic: A green frog: the curve is its body, legs folded, the top tick as a bulging eye.
items.pt: *Rã* means frog in Portuguese and sounds just like **ra**.
items.sound: This r is the Portuguese single r in *caro*. You already have it!
items.tip: ら has a tick on top. う has a dash.

items.story: Two reeds grow by the river. The one on the right is much longer and droops over the water.
items.pic: Two reeds along the strokes with cattail tops; water ripples at the bottom.
items.sound: Again the Portuguese single r, as in *caro*: **ri**.
items.tip: り has a much longer right stroke. い has two even strokes.

items.story: The road zigzags down and ends in a loop: a roundabout at the end of the **rou**te.
items.pic: A road along the stroke with dashed centre line; a roundabout circle at the end loop.
items.tip: る has a loop at the end. ろ does not.

items.story: The left stroke stands firm while the right side kicks its leg out at the end. What a **re**bel!
items.pic: A figure whose last stroke is a kicking leg with a sneaker; motion lines.
items.tip: れ ends with a kick. ね ends in a loop, and わ ends with a curve.

items.story: The same road as る, but it just ends. No loop.
items.pic: A road along the stroke with dashed centre line, ending at a 'road end' sign.
items.tip: ろ has no loop. る has one.

items.story: The left stroke is a person, and the big round curve is their belly after a huge dinner. **Wah!**
items.pic: A person with a big round belly at the curve, a rice bowl, satisfied face.
items.tip: わ ends with a smooth curve. ね loops, and れ kicks.

items.story: The top bar is outstretched arms, the bent middle is the crouching body, and the bottom sweep is the board.
items.pic: A skateboarder: arms along the top bar, crouching body, the bottom stroke as the skateboard with wheels.
items.sound: Pronounced **o**. It is used almost only as the object particle, as in みずを (water).

items.story: It looks like a lowercase **n** written in one quick, flowing stroke.
items.pic: A ghosted lowercase cursive 'n' behind the stroke.
items.sound: At the end of a word it sounds like the nasal ending in Portuguese *bem* or *sim*.
items.tip: ん is a single stroke, like a cursive n.

items.story: The top stroke and hook form the blade, and the long stroke is the handle.
items.pic: An axe: steel blade along the top hooked stroke, wooden handle down the long stroke, wood chips.
items.tip: ア has a short left stroke. マ has a dot.

items.story: One leg leans against the other: a painter's **ea**sel.
items.pic: A painter's easel with a small canvas resting at the junction.
items.tip: イ has two strokes leaning together. ト is a post with one twig.

items.hook: う with a roof: still saying **ooh**!
items.story: The same bowing person as う, now under a roof.
items.pic: A small roof over the top strokes; the bowing body below.
items.tip: ウ has a dash on top. ワ does not.

items.story: The top floor, the shaft, and the ground floor: an **e**levator.
items.pic: An elevator shaft: the vertical is the shaft with a little car, floors at the bars.
items.tip: エ is closed top and bottom. コ is a box corner.

items.story: A figure with arms spread wide on the bar and one leg kicked back to the left. **Oh!**
items.pic: A surprised figure: head above the vertical, arms along the bar, the diagonal as a leg.
items.tip: オ has a diagonal from the middle. ホ has two small feet.

items.story: The same mosquito as か, but quiet this time: it has lost its little dash.
items.pic: The same mosquito idea as か, without buzz lines.
items.tip: カ has no extra dash. か does.

items.story: Two teeth and a shaft: the same **key** as き, ring removed.
items.pic: An antique key shaft with teeth at the bars.
items.tip: キ has two bars. チ has one bar and a slash on top.

items.hook: The **cu**ckoo's beak, with a little cap.
items.story: Like く, but with a short stroke on top like a cap.
items.pic: A bird head with a tiny cap on the short stroke.
items.tip: ク has no inner stroke. タ has a slash inside, and ケ has a long tail.

items.story: It looks like a capital **K** that has slipped sideways: **ke**.
items.pic: A ghosted letter K tilted behind the strokes.
items.tip: ケ has a long downward tail. ク curves.

items.story: Two walls of a box meeting in a **co**rner.
items.pic: The corner of a cardboard box with tape.
items.tip: コ opens to the left. ユ is a U on its side.

items.story: A beam resting on two posts: a simple shrine gate. One post leans as if very old.
items.pic: A small shrine gate in vermilion along the strokes, stone path beneath.
items.tip: サ has two posts. セ has one hooked stroke.

items.story: Two eyes on the left and a smile sweeping **up** from the bottom. **She** is looking at the sky.
items.pic: A face looking up and to the right: dots as eyes, the long stroke as a smile, a little sun top right.
items.tip: シ: the dots are on the left and the long stroke sweeps UP. ツ: the dots are on top and the stroke falls DOWN.

items.story: A skier crouched over their skis, racing down the slope.
items.pic: A skier: head at the top, the hooked stroke as the body, the short stroke as a ski pole, snow.
items.tip: ス has one short stroke. ヌ has a slash through it.

items.story: Like せ, the Sé, but simplified to a single hooked tower.
items.pic: A single cathedral tower on the hooked stroke.
items.pt: It is still the *Sé*, so still **se**.

items.story: Both strokes fall from the top, like a splash and a stream of **so**y sauce.
items.pic: A soy sauce bottle at the top pouring the long stroke; a drop for the short stroke.
items.tip: ソ: both strokes fall from the top. ン: the long stroke sweeps up from the bottom.

items.story: ク is the taco shell, and the slash inside is the filling.
items.pic: A taco shell along the outer strokes with lettuce and filling at the inner slash.
items.tip: タ has a slash inside. ク does not.

items.story: The slash on top is a pom-pom, the bar is outstretched arms, and the long stroke is the body jumping.
items.pic: A cheerleader: pom-pom at the top slash, arms on the bar, skirt flare on the long stroke.
items.sound: Like the Portuguese **tch** in *tchau*.
items.tip: チ has a slash on top. テ has two bars.

items.story: Two drops on top, and the big wave comes crashing DOWN from above.
items.pic: Spray drops on the two short strokes, a wave crashing down along the long stroke.
items.tip: ツ: the dots are on top and the stroke falls DOWN. シ: the dots are on the left and the stroke sweeps UP.

items.story: Two bars and a mast: an old TV aerial on the roof.
items.pic: A TV aerial on a rooftop, little signal arcs.
items.tip: テ has two bars. チ has a slash on top.

items.story: A tall post with one short wing sticking out to the right.
items.pic: A carved totem pole with a single wing on the short stroke.
items.tip: ト has one twig. イ leans.

items.story: A cross with a sweeping blade: a little ナイフ, 'knife'.
items.pic: A kitchen knife: blade along the sweeping stroke, handle at the cross.
items.tip: ナ is a cross. メ is an X.

items.story: Just two lines, exactly like 二 (two).
items.pic: A soft '2' badge behind the two lines.
items.tip: ニ is two lines. コ is a corner, and ミ has three lines.

items.story: The hook is a noodle, and the slash is a chopstick catching it.
items.pic: A pair of chopsticks (the slash) lifting a noodle (the hook), steam.
items.tip: ヌ has a slash crossing it. ス has a short stroke that does not cross.

items.story: The dot is the knot, and the strokes hang down like a necktie.
items.pic: A necktie: knot at the dot, tie body along the strokes, collar points.
items.tip: ネ has a dot on top. ホ does not.

items.story: Just the slash from the 'No' sign, with the circle gone.
items.pic: The slash with a faint circle outline.
items.tip: ノ is one slash. ン and ソ have two strokes.

items.story: Two strokes spreading apart: a pair of **ha**shi, chopsticks, opening.
items.pic: Two chopsticks along the strokes, a grain of rice between them.
items.tip: ハ is two strokes. ル has a kicking right leg.

items.story: A boot seen from the side: the top stroke is its heel, and the long stroke is the sole.
items.pic: A high-heeled boot: heel at the short stroke, sole along the curve.
items.tip: ヒ is angular. ひ is round.

items.story: A flag blown out flat by a strong gust of wind: **fuu**!
items.pic: A flag along the hooked stroke, wind lines blowing.
items.tip: フ has no left stroke. ワ and ウ do.

items.hook: The same little hill as へ.
items.story: Identical to hiragana へ: a hill to **he**ave yourself up.
items.pic: A grassy hill.
items.tip: The same shape as hiragana へ.

items.story: A cross planted in the ground, with a candle burning on each side.
items.pic: A cross along the vertical and bar, two small candles at the side strokes with flames.
items.tip: ホ has two little feet. オ has one diagonal leg.

items.story: The big stroke is the glass on its side, and the dot is the olive rolling out.
items.pic: A tipped martini glass along the main stroke, an olive at the dot.
items.tip: マ has a dot. ア has a longer tail.

items.hook: Three lines for **mi**, the third note.
items.story: Dó, ré, **mi**: three lines for the third note of the scale.
items.pic: Three lines as a small musical staff with a note.
items.pt: Dó-ré-**mi**, the way you learnt it at school in Portugal.
items.tip: ミ has three lines. ニ has two.

items.story: An elbow bent and a fist clenched: a **mu**scle flex.
items.pic: A flexed bicep along the strokes.
items.tip: ム is a closed triangle with a flick. ス is open.

items.story: Two crossed strokes: someone crossed out the **me**ssage.
items.pic: A note paper behind a red X.
items.tip: メ is an X. ナ is a plus sign, and ヌ has a hook.

items.story: The same two worms on the hook as も, drawn with straight lines.
items.pic: A fishing hook with two worms.
items.tip: モ has two bars. テ has its bars on top and no hook.

items.story: Almost exactly like や: a mast and a sail.
items.pic: A sailboat.
items.tip: Almost the same shape as hiragana や.

items.story: A letter **U** knocked over onto its side.
items.pic: A ghosted U rotated beside the strokes.
items.tip: ユ has a long bottom line. コ has a closed corner.

items.story: A capital E facing the wrong way. **Yo**, that's backwards!
items.pic: A ghosted mirrored 'E'.
items.tip: ヨ has three bars. コ has two.

items.story: The top bar is a chopstick, and the hook below is the noodles hanging down.
items.pic: A ramen bowl at the bottom, a chopstick on the top bar, noodles on the hook.
items.sound: The Portuguese single r, as in *caro*.
items.tip: ラ has a separate top bar. フ does not.

items.story: Almost identical to hiragana り.
items.pic: Two reeds.
items.tip: Almost the same shape as hiragana り.

items.story: One leg straight, the other kicking out to jump: a kangaroo (**roo**).
items.pic: Kangaroo legs and a tail along the strokes.
items.tip: ル has a kick on the right. ハ is two plain strokes.

items.story: A big check mark. Everything is **re**ady.
items.pic: A green tick mark.
items.tip: レ is one stroke. ル has two.

items.story: A square box: the head of a ロボット (**ro**botto), 'robot'.
items.pic: A robot head: two eyes and an antenna on the square.
items.tip: ロ is a closed square. コ is open.

items.hook: A ワイン (**wa**in) glass, no stem.
items.story: The bowl of a wine glass seen from the side.
items.pic: Red wine inside the bowl shape.
items.tip: ワ has no dash on top. ウ does.

items.story: Like フ with an extra bar in the middle. You will hardly ever see it, because the particle is written in hiragana (を).
items.pic: A flag (like フ) with an extra crossbar.
items.tip: ヲ has a middle bar. フ does not.

items.story: One dot and one stroke sweeping UP from the bottom.
items.pic: A smiling mouth sweeping up, a single eye.
items.tip: ン: the long stroke sweeps UP. ソ: the long stroke falls DOWN.

items.story: か (ka) + ゛ = **ga**. The two marks turn k → g.
き (ki) + ゛ = **gi**. The two marks turn k → g.
く (ku) + ゛ = **gu**. The two marks turn k → g.
け (ke) + ゛ = **ge**. The two marks turn k → g.
こ (ko) + ゛ = **go**. The two marks turn k → g.
さ (sa) + ゛ = **za**. The two marks turn s → z.
し (shi) + ゛ = **ji**. The two marks turn s → z (shi becomes ji).
す (su) + ゛ = **zu**. The two marks turn s → z.
せ (se) + ゛ = **ze**. The two marks turn s → z.
そ (so) + ゛ = **zo**. The two marks turn s → z.
た (ta) + ゛ = **da**. The two marks turn t → d.
ち (chi) + ゛ = **ji**. The two marks turn s → z (shi becomes ji).
items.sound: Sounds the same as じ and is rare. It appears in a few words like はなぢ (nosebleed).

items.story: つ (tsu) + ゛ = **zu**. The two marks turn s → z.
items.sound: Sounds the same as ず and is rare. It appears in a few words like はなぢ (nosebleed).

items.story: て (te) + ゛ = **de**. The two marks turn t → d.
と (to) + ゛ = **do**. The two marks turn t → d.
は (ha) + ゛ = **ba**. The two marks turn h → b.
ひ (hi) + ゛ = **bi**. The two marks turn h → b.
ふ (fu) + ゛ = **bu**. The two marks turn h → b.
へ (he) + ゛ = **be**. The two marks turn h → b.
ほ (ho) + ゛ = **bo**. The two marks turn h → b.
は (ha) + ゜ = **pa**. The little circle turn h → p.
ひ (hi) + ゜ = **pi**. The little circle turn h → p.
ふ (fu) + ゜ = **pu**. The little circle turn h → p.
へ (he) + ゜ = **pe**. The little circle turn h → p.
ほ (ho) + ゜ = **po**. The little circle turn h → p.
カ (ka) + ゛ = **ga**. The two marks turn k → g.
キ (ki) + ゛ = **gi**. The two marks turn k → g.
ク (ku) + ゛ = **gu**. The two marks turn k → g.
ケ (ke) + ゛ = **ge**. The two marks turn k → g.
コ (ko) + ゛ = **go**. The two marks turn k → g.
サ (sa) + ゛ = **za**. The two marks turn s → z.
シ (shi) + ゛ = **ji**. The two marks turn s → z (shi becomes ji).
ス (su) + ゛ = **zu**. The two marks turn s → z.
セ (se) + ゛ = **ze**. The two marks turn s → z.
ソ (so) + ゛ = **zo**. The two marks turn s → z.

lessons.intro: Japanese has just five vowels, and they are pure, like Portuguese stressed vowels. Every other kana is built on them.

lessons.d: Two little marks: g and z
lessons.intro: Add two little marks (゛, called dakuten) and the sound becomes voiced: k → g, s → z. No new shapes to learn!

lessons.d: d, b and the little circle
lessons.intro: The same marks turn t → d and h → b. A little circle (゜) turns h → p. ぢ and づ sound like じ and ず and are rare.
A big kana ending in -i plus a small ゃ ゅ ょ blends into one beat: き + ゃ = きゃ (kya). It is one beat, not two.
More of the same blending pattern. Remember: the small kana is written half size.
Voiced versions of the same combinations. You already know every piece.
Katakana spells foreign words and names. Same sounds as hiragana, sharper shapes. Many look like their hiragana twin.
Small vowels let katakana write sounds Japanese didn't have, like fa, ti and we. Also: ー makes the vowel before it long (コーヒー).

sounds.title: Five pure vowels
sounds.body: Japanese has only five vowels, each short and pure. You already know them from Portuguese stressed vowels. There are no English-style glides like 'ay' or 'oh-oo'.

sounds.title: One kana, one beat
sounds.body: Japanese is timed in beats called morae. Every kana gets the same length, and so do ん and small っ. Tap and count the beats.
items: 4 beats: Tokyo is longer than it looks

sounds.title: Long vowels change the meaning
sounds.body: Holding a vowel for an extra beat makes a different word. Listen to each pair.

sounds.title: Small っ: a silent beat
sounds.body: A small っ means a short silent pause, as if you hold your breath for one beat before the next consonant.

sounds.title: Swallowed vowels
sounds.body: Between or after voiceless consonants, i and u are often whispered. です sounds like 'dess'. European Portuguese does this too: think how *telefone* is said in Lisbon.

sounds.title: Pitch, not stress
sounds.body: Japanese words rise and fall in pitch instead of having a stressed syllable. Same kana, different pitch, different word.

sounds.title: The Japanese r
sounds.body: ら り る れ ろ use a quick tap of the tongue: exactly the single r in Portuguese *caro* or *para*. English speakers find this hard. You don't.

sounds.title: Two new sounds: fu and tsu
sounds.body: ふ is a soft blow between f and h, as if cooling soup. つ starts like the ts in *tsé-tsé*.
